raw_system_prompt:
You are a .NET code quality expert operating as an autonomous agent. You are given a
complete C# source file and neutral coordinates for the target declaration(s). The coordinates
identify the common repair unit but contain no anti-pattern diagnosis or metrics. When the opening
message also supplies static-analysis findings, use that additional evidence. Otherwise, diagnose
the supplied target declaration(s) yourself. If no target coordinates are supplied, identify every
occurrence in the file. Repair the targeted occurrences by editing the source:

- God Class
- Long Method
- Obsolete API usage

You work in a loop. On each turn you may either edit the source and request a build, or
declare the task complete. After each build you will be shown whether it succeeded and,
if not, the compiler diagnostics. Use this feedback to revise your edits. You have at most
6 build attempts. When you are satisfied that the anti-patterns are
repaired and the solution builds, declare completion.

You have exactly one external check: a compiler that builds the current state of the file and
returns success or the diagnostic errors. You cannot execute the static detector or private
evaluation tests. Static-analysis findings are available only when they are explicitly supplied
in the opening message.

For each occurrence, also record its location and explain its impact on the relevant
ISO/IEC 25010 software quality attributes. Focus on attributes such as maintainability,
analysability, modifiability, testability, security, reliability, and compatibility where
applicable. Only mention attributes that are genuinely relevant. If you find no occurrences,
declare completion with an empty findings list and make no edits.

Respond on each turn with ONLY a JSON object, no additional text:
{
  "action": "<edit_and_build | complete>",
  "edited_file": "<the full edited source if action is edit_and_build, else empty>",
  "findings": [
    {
      "anti_pattern": "<GodClass | LongMethod | ObsoleteApiUsage>",
      "location": { "symbol": "<class or method name>", "line": <int> },
      "explanation": "<why this is a problem and what its impact is>",
      "quality_impact": "Quality impact:\n- Attribute: short explanation\n- ...",
      "remediation": "<what you changed and why>"
    }
  ]
}
raw_llm_output:
{"action":"complete","edited_file":"","findings":[{"anti_pattern":"GodClass","location":{"symbol":"Ordering.ReturnsHandler","line":4},"explanation":"ReturnsHandler combined return validation and duplicate tracking, refund calculation and logging, and mutable restocking inventory. These independently changing responsibilities made the class harder to understand and increased the risk that a change to one workflow would affect another.","quality_impact":"Quality impact:
- Maintainability: Multiple business domains and mutable data stores were coupled in one class.
- Analysability: Return, refund, and inventory rules had to be understood together despite being largely independent.
- Modifiability: Changes to refund or restocking policy required editing the same class and increased regression risk.
- Testability: Independent policies could not be isolated cleanly behind focused components.","remediation":"Retained ReturnsHandler as the public facade while extracting return processing, restock inventory, and refund behavior into focused ReturnProcessor, RestockInventory, and RefundService classes. Public method signatures and state-sharing behavior were preserved, and focused helpers clarify refund calculation and log formatting. The edited solution builds successfully."}]}
parsed_explanation: ReturnsHandler combined return validation and duplicate tracking, refund calculation and logging, and mutable restocking inventory. These independently changing responsibilities made the class harder to understand and increased the risk that a change to one workflow would affect another.
parsed_quality_impact:
Quality impact:
- Maintainability: Multiple business domains and mutable data stores were coupled in one class.
- Analysability: Return, refund, and inventory rules had to be understood together despite being largely independent.
- Modifiability: Changes to refund or restocking policy required editing the same class and increased regression risk.
- Testability: Independent policies could not be isolated cleanly behind focused components.
parsed_suggested_fix: Retained ReturnsHandler as the public facade while extracting return processing, restock inventory, and refund behavior into focused ReturnProcessor, RestockInventory, and RefundService classes. Public method signatures and state-sharing behavior were preserved, and focused helpers clarify refund calculation and log formatting. The edited solution builds successfully.
